classes.label: T6 PX Mk1 (2011–2015)
key_visual_features: Trapezoidal headlights with chrome inner surround
Single horizontal chrome bar across grille
More upright, narrower front fascia compared to Mk2
Round or oval fog light housings in lower bumper
Flat bonnet with minimal character lines
Smaller overall grille opening
rear_features: RANGER lettering across tailgate in chrome
Simpler tail light cluster without LED elements
Ford oval badge centred on tailgate
side_features: Flatter door panels with minimal sculpting
Smaller side mirrors compared to later models
classes.distinguishing_tips: Mk1 has a more conservative, upright grille. The headlight shape is trapezoidal with a notable chrome inner surround. The overall front end looks narrower and taller than the Mk2/3.

classes.label: T6 PX Mk2/Mk3 Mainstream (2015–2022)
key_visual_features: Revised wider and more aggressive grille opening
Updated headlights with revised inner graphics (not trapezoidal)
More pronounced bonnet creases and character lines
Wider lower bumper with horizontal split
Revised fog light position and housing shape
Overall wider, lower stance than Mk1
rear_features: Updated tail light cluster with different graphics to Mk1
Similar tailgate layout but with revised proportions
side_features: Subtle body crease running front to rear
classes.distinguishing_tips: Mk2/3 mainstream has a wider, more aggressive look than Mk1 but lacks the flared arches and RAPTOR badging of the Raptor. Check the grille width and headlight shape — wider and more dynamic than Mk1.

classes.label: T6 PX Mk3 Raptor (2018–2022)
key_visual_features: RAPTOR lettering across centre of grille (most distinctive feature)
Honeycomb mesh grille pattern — no horizontal bar
Dramatically flared wheel arches (wider body)
Skid plate integrated into front bumper
Recovery points visible on front bumper
Wider overall stance than mainstream Mk3
rear_features: RAPTOR lettering across tailgate in large block letters
Same tail light cluster as Mk3 mainstream but wider body
side_features: Flared wheel arch extensions — most visible distinguishing feature from side
Wider track visibly evident from side
classes.distinguishing_tips: The Raptor is unmistakable from the front due to RAPTOR lettering and honeycomb grille. From the side the flared arches are the giveaway. Never confuse with mainstream Mk3 — the body is visibly wider.

classes.label: Next Gen PY/RA Mainstream (2022–present)
key_visual_features: Completely new body style — not an evolution of T6
C-shaped LED daytime running lights
Wide horizontal grille with thick upper bar
More upright windscreen and squarer cab shape
RANGER lettering across grille (not ford oval centre)
Wider front end with more aggressive proportions than old shape
rear_features: Full-width LED tail light bar connecting both sides
RANGER lettering across tailgate in large block letters
side_features: More upright A-pillar and squarer greenhouse
Different body crease pattern to T6
classes.distinguishing_tips: Next Gen mainstream is unmistakably different from the old T6 shape. The C-shaped DRLs are the quickest identifier. Distinguished from Next Gen Raptor by absence of flared arches and RAPTOR badging.

classes.label: Next Gen PY/RA Raptor (2022–present)
key_visual_features: RAPTOR lettering across front grille
Honeycomb grille mesh — no horizontal bar
Flared wheel arches (wider than Next Gen mainstream)
More aggressive bumper with integrated skid plate
Wider overall stance than mainstream Next Gen
C-shaped LED DRLs present but in wider front end
rear_features: Full-width LED tail light bar same as mainstream
side_features: Flared arch extensions — distinguishes from mainstream Next Gen
classes.distinguishing_tips: Same as T6 Raptor rule — look for RAPTOR lettering and flared arches. The Next Gen Raptor is wider than the Next Gen mainstream. From the front the grille is honeycomb mesh not horizontal bar.
